title: skillscope skill machine requirements
description: Optional file at <skill>/evals/machine.yml, present ONLY for a skill whose behavioral cases need something the everyday runners do not give them: fewer platforms, particular hardware, a sandbox of its own, or prerequisites to provide. Absent means none of those, which is the common case. Say which platforms to use and which runner labels the work needs; what follows from asking for hardware -- the base runs-on labels, the pull-request label rationing that pool, the environment holding its credentials -- belongs to the repo and is passed to skillscope by the workflow, not restated here.

os.description: Which platforms to exercise, as runner labels: Linux, Windows, or macOS. Defaults to the workflow's `behavior_os`. Narrow it for a skill that shells out to platform-specific tooling.

labels.description: Extra `runs-on` labels the behavioral cases need, added to the base labels the workflow supplies. Name the hardware, not the pool: `mi300x` says what the skill requires and lands it on any runner registered with that label. A leg that asks for labels is treated as scoped, so it is also what the repo may hold behind a gate label and pay for from a separate environment. Keep the list as short as the runners allow -- every label is a condition a pool has to satisfy, and a label no runner carries is a job that queues forever rather than an error.

sandbox.description: Compose file, resolved beside this machine.yml in evals/, describing the sandbox the behavioral cases need under `--engine claude-code`. Absent means the default container with no network, which is what a skill that only reads and writes files should want. Name one to opt into network egress -- a skill that installs a server or pulls a model cannot run without it -- or to bind a device in. Ignored on Windows, where inspect's sandbox layer assumes a POSIX guest and cases run unsandboxed on the host instead.

prerequisites.description: What the behavioral cases need provided before they run, applied by every engine where its agent runs: once per skill on the host under the default engine, in each case's container under `--engine claude-code`. Each runs `check`; if that fails, `install` runs and `check` is retried with `env` applied, and only then is `env` handed to the agent. A prerequisite whose `check` passes is used as is and none of its `env` is applied. On the host, steps run with the directory holding this file as their working directory; in a container, in `/opt/skillscope/steps`, which holds only the files they name. Steps see `SKILL_SOURCE_DIR` (the skill's source tree; host only) and `SKILL_CACHE_DIR` (scratch space, removed after the skill on the host; `/opt/skillscope/cache` in a container, so an image can bake an install in at the same path).

name.description: What this provides, as reports should name it. Unique within the file.

check.description: Exits 0 when the prerequisite is present. Files it names are copied into a container the same way as for `install`.

install.description: Provides the prerequisite. Under `--engine claude-code`, an argv item that is a path to a file in the directory holding this machine.yml, or below it, is copied into the container at the same relative path for the step and removed before the agent starts; a file mentioned only inside a string is not, and a step naming an eval dataset is refused.

env.description: Set for the agent once the prerequisite has been installed. A value replaces the variable rather than extending it. Values may refer to `${SKILL_SOURCE_DIR}` and `${SKILL_CACHE_DIR}`, and no other `$` may appear; names the harness sets for the agent (`ANTHROPIC_*`, `CLAUDE_*`, `IS_SANDBOX`) are refused. The skillscope parser enforces those rules, a command for every platform in `os`, and unique names, none of which this schema expresses.

command.description: An argv, or a mapping from platform (`linux`, `windows`, `macos`) to argv. A container is always `linux`.
